channel.title: East New York Times
channel.description: Independent community news for East New York, Cypress Hills, City Line, Starrett City and Brownsville, Brooklyn.

item.title: Medicaid Work Rules Start Jan. 1. Here's How to Check Where You Stand.
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: A free city tool walks you through the new SNAP and Medicaid rules one question at a time. If you're exempt, you may still have to prove it.

item.title: The Tax Lien Sale Is Coming Back. Here's What East New York Homeowners Should Know Now.
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: City officials told the Council the sale will return in 2027 with new protections. But East New York homeowners still pay about twice Park Slope's effective property tax rate, and the city has no reform bill yet.

item.title: Can a Building Violation Put Your Home at Risk? Council Takes Up Homeowner Protections Tuesday
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: A joint Council hearing will weigh bills to warn owners before unpaid Buildings Department fines turn into tax liens, enroll homeowners in property tax payment plans automatically and study who gets hit hardest by violations.

item.title: East New York's Midterm Results: From Albany to Washington
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: A look at who East New York voters chose in Albany and Washington and what the preliminary results mean for residents.

item.title: New Vendor Licenses Are Coming. East New York Vendors Want a Fair Shot.
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: The city is adding 10,500 general vendor licenses, and the waitlist is open now. On Fountain Avenue, vendors say they're ready to go legal.

item.title: $1.8 Million Paid. A Church Still at Risk.
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: Citadel Cathedral leaders say their foreclosure fight exposes a broader concern: financing arrangements and barriers that can leave Black congregations vulnerable to losing their property.

item.title: Wharton Place Rezoning Draws Tough Questions on Affordability and Neighborhood Fit at CB5 Hearing
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: A proposal to rezone 17 and 21 Wharton Place for a seven-story, 73-unit building drew pushback from Community Board 5’s Land Use and Housing Committee over affordability, building size and whether it fits the surrounding neighborhood.

item.title: East New York’s Innovative Urban Village Opens Its First Affordable Homes
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: The first phase of Innovative Urban Village has opened on the Christian Cultural Center campus in East New York, delivering 385 permanently affordable homes. Gov. Kathy Hochul, Mayor Zohran Mamdani and project partners marked the opening last week.

item.title: Rooted in East New York 5K Supports Scholarships and Community Programs
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson, Michael Johnson, Catherine Hanao
item.description: Cypress Hills Local Development Corporation’s junior board hosted its second annual community 5K at Highland Park, raising money for scholarships for East New York youth headed to trade school, two-year colleges and four-year schools.

item.title: Assemblywoman Nikki Lucas Claims Brooklyn Democratic Party Chair, but Courts May Decide Whether It Counts
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson, Nikki Lucas, Rodneyse Bichotte Hermelyn, Julio Peña III, Nydia Velázquez
item.description: Assemblywoman Nikki Lucas was named Brooklyn Democratic Party chair in a late-night vote that reformers call illegal. Here’s the court fight and what’s next.

item.title: East New York Farms Youth Grow Food for Their Community
item.dc:creator: Lilly Sabella, Heavenleiann Schuler, Joshua John, Matthew John, Ariella Riapos
item.description: At a half-acre urban farm in Brooklyn, teen interns weed garlic beds, make compost and stock a farmers’ market with crops familiar to the neighborhood’s immigrant families — learning about food access, and themselves, along the way.

item.title: NYCHA Worker Leighton Brown Killed by Falling Tree at Cypress Hills Houses
item.dc:creator: Leighton Brown, Chris Banks, Zohran Mamdani
item.description: The 56-year-old died after a tree struck him in an East New York parking lot Saturday; residents remember his service to the development.

item.title: “Who Invented That? We Invented That”: East New York Youth Parade Celebrates Black Innovation
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson, Keron Alleyne, George Franklin Grant, Kelley Pierre, Inez Barron
item.description: Students, teachers, families and community groups marched through East New York for the fifth annual Black Inventors Youth Parade, turning neighborhood streets into a public lesson in Black history and invention.

item.title: More Than a Concert: East New York’s Four-Day Wellness Series Brings Music, Resources and Community Together
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson, Nikki Lucas, Keith Watkins, Bri Babineaux
item.description: Assemblywoman Nikki Lucas and DJ Keith Watkins’ annual East New York Concert + Wellness Series returned for its fourth year with four days of music, health screenings, food vendors and community resources.

item.title: “Say his name”: East New York tenants and Council Member Chris Banks put a landlord on notice at 255 Pennsylvania Avenue
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson, Chris Banks
item.description: About 60 residents of a 24-unit rent-stabilized building — some there more than 30 years — say Plaza Management fixes the surface and leaves the cause. One tenant who helped organize says the response was a 14-day eviction notice.

item.title: A Broken Front Door, a Worst-Landlord Ranking, and Tenants Who Refuse to Leave
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson, Sandy Nurse, Kim Council, Joseph Safdie
item.description: Residents of 2342 Atlantic Ave. rally with Council Member Sandy Nurse and Deputy Borough President Kim Council, demanding HPD action against a landlord with 1,148 lifetime violations across the property.

item.title: Brooklyn’s Democratic Rules Change Passed. The Court Fight and Chair Vote Come Next.
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: A closed vote in Mill Basin expanded the Kings County Democratic Party’s executive committee from 42 to 68 members “by narrow margins.” Reformers backing Julio Peña III said they would refile suit Wednesday morning.

item.title: Brooklyn Democrats Move to Reshape Their Own Rules Tonight — What It Means for East New York
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: The Kings County Democratic Party’s executive committee votes tonight on a 10-amendment package that would expand its own membership to more than 68 voting members before this fall’s chair election.

item.title: Fat Boys Avenue, Down by Law
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: East New York co-named Schenck Avenue “Fat Boys Avenue” on August 22, 2026. Kool Rock-Ski, DMC and Council Member Chris Banks on why the sign matters.

item.title: Fifty Years on One Block: How Virginia Burroughs Became a Street
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: A tenants association president who served half a century at Essex Terrace is now the name at Linwood Street and Hegeman Avenue.

item.title: "Sometimes That Part Means Walking Off in Handcuffs": Christian Celeste Tate on What He's Taking to Albany
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: Our full sit-down with the incoming Assembly Member for AD-54: the two ICE arrests, the day job advising billionaires, and why he doesn't think elected officials build movements.

item.title: The Real NYCHA Story Is Not Public vs. Private. It’s Who Answers When the Ceiling Comes Down.
item.dc:creator: Delaine Dixon, MPA I/O
item.description: A policy writer responds to East New York Times coverage of Councilmember Chris Banks's warning on PACT and focuses the debate on enforceable accountability.

item.title: Only 13 Nearby Residents Hired on $400 Million Broadway Junction Project, Local Officials Say
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: Local officials say only 13 residents from the eight ZIP codes surrounding Broadway Junction have been hired on the MTA's $400 million project.

item.title: Banks Calls for New NYCHA Leadership and Warns Against Public Housing Privatization
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: Council Member Chris Banks said funding alone will not solve NYCHA’s problems and argued that traditional public housing must be preserved.

item.title: Constituent Pop Ups Pull Up Across BKLYN’s 37th District
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: Dominique Alexandre explains how Council Member Sandy Nurse’s office helps District 37 residents navigate housing, sanitation, and city bureaucracy.

item.title: “No Reason for These Takeovers”: New NYPD Youth Commander Pitches a Reset at East New York’s Community Hub
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: Captain Lori Perez, the NYPD officer now overseeing Youth Strategies at 127 Pennsylvania Avenue, told CB5 she wants to restore the building and bring youth programming back to East New York.

item.title: “No Attendance, You Won’t Be on the Board”: CB5 Chair Alice Lowman Draws a Line on Non-Attendance and Borough
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: At Community Board 5’s last general board meeting of the session, Chair Alice Lowman warned that non-attendance could reshape the board in September.

item.title: Nikki Lucas Connects Albany Budget Fights to East New York’s Housing, Schools and Jobs
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: At Community Board 5’s final meeting of the session, Assemblymember Nikki Lucas explained how state budget and legislative work are landing in East New York, Starrett City and Brownsville.

item.title: Governor and Brooklyn DA Charge 23 Alleged Gang Members in 176-Count Case — What It Means for East New York
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: The Governor and Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez announced a 176-count case against 23 alleged gang members in Brooklyn, including conspiracy to commit murder and weapons charges. Here is why East New York — and the 75th Precinct — should be paying attention.

item.title: Housing, Wealth, and Who Gets to Stay in East New York
item.dc:creator: Deric Johnson
item.description: At CB5’s final meeting of the season, Sandy Nurse pressed for housing vouchers, NYCHA repairs, and homeownership pathways while East New York’s next Assembly member, Christian Celeste Tate, watched from the audience.
